findings.defective_text: Reject splitting the sea-bound and rain-giver illustrations (Jer.5.22 / Jer.5.23-Jer.5.24) at the point WEB's translation closes its quotation mark: that convention is translational apparatus, not a textual seam attested in the Hebrew, where no formula, vocative, or imperative marks that point.
findings.byte_evidence: The translation-layer fact is true - WEB Jer.5.22 ends its nested single quotation at the verse close and Jer.5.23 opens a fresh double quotation behind a paragraph break (tier-4 layout, para_before true at Jer.5.23) - but the rejection makes that tier-4 convention the whole ground of the row's strongest rival, and the tier-1 signal standing at the same junction goes unweighed: שִׁמְעוּ נָ֣א זֹ֔את עַ֥ם סָכָ֖ל (oshb:Jer.5.21, byte tier) and הַאוֹתִ֨י לֹא תִירָ֜אוּ (oshb:Jer.5.22, byte tier) address the hearers in the second person, while וְלָעָ֤ם הַזֶּה֙ הָיָ֔ה (oshb:Jer.5.23, byte tier) turns to third-person description of the people. The rejection's negative sweep names three device classes - formula, vocative, imperative - and a grammatical-person shift falls outside all three, so defeating the punctuation rival does not establish that Jer.5.22 holds with Jer.5.23-Jer.5.24.
findings.proposed_cure: Re-ground the first rejection sentence on the second-to-third-person shift at the Jer.5.22 / Jer.5.23 junction and say why the commissioned proclamation carries across it, leaving the quotation-mark convention as a disclosed tier-4 non-signal rather than the rival's ground.

findings.defective_text: the byte difference between the two clauses is the tsevaot expansion
findings.byte_evidence: At the tier the sentence names, the two opening runs differ in three accent codepoints besides the tsevaot expansion: כֹּֽה (oshb:Jer.11.21, byte tier) carries U+05BD where כֹּ֤ה (oshb:Jer.11.22, byte tier) carries U+05A4; אָמַ֤ר (oshb:Jer.11.21, byte tier) carries U+05A4 where אָמַר֙ (oshb:Jer.11.22, byte tier) carries U+0599; יְהוָה֙ (oshb:Jer.11.21, byte tier) carries U+0599 where יְהוָ֣ה (oshb:Jer.11.22, byte tier) carries U+05A3. The four opening words match at the consonantal-skeleton tier and not at byte tier, and the residue beyond those accents is the צְבָא֔וֹת (oshb:Jer.11.22, byte tier) expansion.
findings.proposed_cure: Retier the sentence to the consonantal-skeleton tier, where the residue between the two opening runs is the tsevaot expansion.

findings.defective_text: matching “Jeremiah said, Yahweh’s word came to me, saying,” (web:Jer.32.6)
findings.byte_evidence: WEB Jer.32.6 sets an opening double quotation mark before Yahweh’s: the verse reads Jeremiah said, then that opening mark, then Yahweh’s word came to me, saying,. The row's curly-quoted run silently drops that nested opening mark, so the run is not a verbatim WEB quotation; the alteration flattens exactly the translation-layer quotation structure this unit elsewhere disclaims as formatting.
findings.proposed_cure: Re-cut the quoted run so it reproduces WEB's own quotation marks, or stop the quotation before the nested opening mark.

findings.defective_text: Ishmael remains the sole actor through verse 10
findings.byte_evidence: The exclusivity carries no sweep and the row's own splices contradict it inside the same span: וַיָּבֹ֣אוּ אֲ֠נָשִׁים (oshb:Jer.41.5, byte tier) makes the arriving pilgrims the acting subject, and וַיֹּאמְר֤וּ אֶל יִשְׁמָעֵאל֙ (oshb:Jer.41.8, byte tier) makes the ten men the speaking subject. Both verses are spliced in this row's own rationale, so the claim fails against evidence the row itself carries.
findings.proposed_cure: Narrow the claim to the Jer.41.9 / Jer.41.10 junction, where no new subject is introduced, rather than extending it across the span.

findings.defective_text: the setumah closing this verse corroborates reading it with what precedes rather than with Johanan's pursuit that follows
findings.byte_evidence: The same mark at oshb:Jer.41.10 is handled two incompatible ways in one row: the rejection field claims corroboration force for the adopted reading, while the device field states that the closing mark at this same verse is disclosed as texture, single-witness, without corroboration force claimed for the reading adopted or against it. The rejection field also carries the corroboration claim without the single-witness / tier-3 label the parashah layer requires on each citation in the Prophets.
findings.proposed_cure: Settle the row on one handling of the closing mark at oshb:Jer.41.10 and carry the single-witness tier-3 label in whichever field claims any force for it.

findings.defective_text: the impression of a second mouth rests only on the nested single quotation the English rendering opens at 51:10 and not at 51:9, a tier-4 punctuation fact disclaimed here rather than read as evidence
findings.byte_evidence: The punctuation fact itself is true (WEB opens a nested single quotation at Jer.51.10 and a double at Jer.51.9), but the exclusivity is false at the bytes, so the disclaimer carries the whole rejection of the internal split: עִזְב֕וּהָ וְנֵלֵ֖ךְ אִ֣ישׁ לְאַרְצ֑וֹ (oshb:Jer.51.9, byte tier; that verse carries one ketiv/qere note, single-witness, on its opening verb, outside this splice) sends each speaker to his own separate land, while בֹּ֚אוּ וּנְסַפְּרָ֣ה בְצִיּ֔וֹן אֶֽת מַעֲשֵׂ֖ה יְהוָ֥ה אֱלֹהֵֽינוּ (oshb:Jer.51.10, byte tier) turns to one named homeland and a covenant title - אִ֣ישׁ לְאַרְצ֑וֹ (oshb:Jer.51.9, byte tier) against בְצִיּ֔וֹן (oshb:Jer.51.10, byte tier) is a Hebrew-side ground for the second-mouth reading standing beside the punctuation. The rationale field also tags oshb:Jer.51.9 and oshb:Jer.51.10 at byte tier and calls them spliced, yet that field exhibits no splice from either verse, which leaves the tier-4 punctuation fact carrying the juncture.
findings.proposed_cure: Splice both verses and weigh the separate-lands / one-homeland contrast on the bytes, dropping the exclusivity so the punctuation is disclosed as a tier-4 non-signal rather than named as the rival's ground.

findings.defective_text: the returning exiles' own words (rationale) against its shift to a first-person foreign speaker (rejection) and The quoted foreign voice is embedded speech (device notes)
findings.byte_evidence: One first-person-plural voice at oshb:Jer.51.9-oshb:Jer.51.10 is named two incompatible ways inside one row - returning exiles in the rationale, a foreign speaker in the rejection and device fields - and the identification is exactly what the internal-split question turns on, since אִ֣ישׁ לְאַרְצ֑וֹ (oshb:Jer.51.9, byte tier) and בְצִיּ֔וֹן (oshb:Jer.51.10, byte tier) pull the two readings apart.
findings.proposed_cure: Name the mouth once, from the bytes, and use the same identification in the rationale, the rejection and the device notes.

findings.defective_text: the rationale run quoting WEB Jer.41.6 whole, with WEB's own nested double quotation inside the row's outer curly pair
findings.byte_evidence: WEB Jer.41.6 itself sets a nested double quotation around the summons to Gedaliah, so quoting the verse whole inside another curly double pair opens a double before any close; the pair scanner then cannot see any quoted run in that field, and the field's other WEB quotations sit outside verbatim coverage.
findings.proposed_cure: Re-cut the quoted run to stop before WEB's nested quotation so the field's pairing closes and its quoted runs stay inside verbatim coverage.
